title: Self-help diagnostics: which admin tests explain a broken setting, and who can run them?
summary: Hold: the table reports automation as undocumented even though Microsoft documents PowerShell equivalents for Information Protection and some Exchange diagnostics. The Graph role requirement also needs its delegated-access qualification, and the data-processing statements must distinguish Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostics from Purview Help-pane diagnostics.

claims.claim: Purview role-group members can be added through Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes to view and manage compliance and governance roles in your organization. ... Select Role groups. ... On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member <member> adds a member to a management role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group.
claims.fix: Add the Microsoft pages relied on but missing from sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/add-rolegroupmember, https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync, and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/error-responses. The existing eDiscovery docs link contains the printed Add-RoleGroupMember operation and can remain.

claims.claim: Editing Purview role groups requires the Role management role.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal by using credentials for an admin account assigned the Role management role.

claims.claim: Membership of qualifying Purview role groups controls access to DLP and Information Protection diagnostics.
claims.quote: A role group is a set of roles that enable users to do their jobs across compliance and governance solutions in the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Compliance Administrator ... Mapped Purview role groups ... Compliance Administrator

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin roles are assigned through Roles > Role assignments > role > Assigned > Add users.
claims.quote: To view the administrator roles available for your organization, choose the Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange, Intune, or Billing tab. ... On the Assigned tab, select Add users or Add groups.
claims.fix: For the Microsoft 365 directory roles discussed here, expand the path to 'Roles > Role assignments > Microsoft Entra ID > role > Assigned > Add users'. The omitted tab selects the list of roles, so this is not a wrong destination.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments creates a directory role assignment.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments ... "roleDefinitionId": "c2cf284d-6c41-4e6b-afac-4b80928c9034", "principalId": "f8ca5a85-489a-49a0-b555-0a6d81e56f0d", "directoryScopeId": "/"
claims.fix: Keep the call and add to its note: 'The request body identifies the assigned role with roleDefinitionId and the recipient with principalId; directoryScopeId specifies the scope.'

claims.claim: Creating a directory role assignment through Microsoft Graph requires Privileged Role Administrator at least.
claims.quote: For delegated access using work or school accounts, the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role or a custom role that grants the permissions required for this operation. Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged role supported for this operation.
claims.fix: Replace both role statements with: 'For delegated access using work or school accounts, Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged supported built-in role; a custom role granting the required permissions is also supported.' The reference also supports application access with RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory, so do not state this signed-in-user role requirement for all calls.

claims.claim: Purview DLP file diagnostics are reached through Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Diagnostics.
claims.quote: You can find these diagnostics on the following portal pages: ... Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Diagnostics

claims.claim: Test-DlpPolicies -workload <workload> -Fileurl <path/direct link> -SendReportTo <smtpaddress> tests which DLP policies match an item.
claims.quote: After you have the site ID and the direct link path, run the cmdlet to test your policies. ... Test-DlpPolicies -workload <workload> -Fileurl <path/direct link> -SendReportTo <smtpaddress>

claims.claim: Information Protection diagnostics are reached through Solutions > Information Protection > Diagnostics.
claims.quote: You can find these diagnostics on the following portal pages: ... Solutions > Information Protection > Diagnostics

claims.claim: Automation for label, label-policy, auto-labeling and email-encryption checks is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Use the Test-IRMConfiguration cmdlet to test Information Rights Management (IRM) configuration and functionality. ... Test-IRMConfiguration -Sender chris@fabrikam.com -Recipient michell@fourthcoffee.com
claims.fix: Replace controls[3].api with kind 'powershell', call 'Test-IRMConfiguration -Sender <sender-email-address> -Recipient <recipient-email-address>', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/test-irmconfiguration'. Append to the existing note: 'This call covers the IRM configuration and functionality check, not all label checks.' The cited Purview diagnostics page explicitly maps email-encryption checks to this cmdlet.

claims.claim: Information Protection Solutions-page diagnostics require Compliance Administrator or Security Administrator.
claims.quote: To run the Information Protection diagnostics, you need to have either of the following roles: Compliance Administrator; Security Administrator
claims.fix: Keep the roles supported by the cited Purview-specific article. Add this qualification in Governance controls and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/microsoft-365/diagnostics/purview-compliance-diagnostics: 'Microsoft's alternate self-help diagnostics article states that Solutions-page diagnostics require a Microsoft 365 global administrator; the Purview-specific article instead lists Compliance Administrator or Security Administrator for Information Protection and a wider role list for DLP.'

claims.claim: DLP Solutions-page diagnostics accept roles including Organization Configuration, View-Only Configuration, Security Reader, DLP Compliance Management and Information Protection Analyst.
claims.quote: To run the DLP diagnostics, you need to have any of the following roles: ... Organization Configuration; View-Only Configuration; Security Reader; DLP Compliance Management ... Information Protection Analyst

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risks and limits: Gradual rollout
claims.claim: Purview Solutions-page diagnostics are rolling out gradually and might not yet be available in a tenant.
claims.quote: Diagnostics on Solutions pages are being rolled out gradually and might not yet be available in your organization.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Help-pane diagnostics are reached through Help > describe the issue > select an option > Run Tests.
claims.quote: Select the Help icon ... enter a brief description of the issue ... Select one of the listed options ... If the selected option has an associated diagnostic, enter any requested information, and then select Run Tests
claims.fix: The pre-check's missing phrases are descriptions of documented actions, not invented labels. Keep the route, but add to the note: 'The Exchange diagnostics article describes the entry point as Help & support; the Purview diagnostics article describes the Help icon.' Both cited pages support the experience but use different entry-point labels.

claims.claim: Automation for running the Help-pane diagnostics covered by this Purview, Exchange, SharePoint and Teams row is not yet documented.
claims.quote: However, a subset of these diagnostics can be accessed by using Exchange Online PowerShell or the Exchange admin center (EAC). ... Company Object ... Invoke-ProvisioningCompanyObjectDiagnostic
claims.fix: Replace controls[4].api with kind 'powershell', call 'Invoke-ProvisioningCompanyObjectDiagnostic', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/invoke-provisioningcompanyobjectdiagnostic'. Append to its note: 'Automation shown covers the Exchange company-object diagnostic only, not a general API for the Help pane; see its reference for permissions and limits.' The reference documents this parameterless operation as validating core Microsoft 365 tenant information.

claims.claim: Self-help diagnostics are administrator-run tests available in the Microsoft 365 admin center and Microsoft Purview portal to investigate configuration problems.
claims.quote: You can run diagnostics to identify and resolve issues in Microsoft Purview. ... Microsoft Purview portal ... On Solutions pages ... In the Help pane ... Microsoft 365 admin center ... In the Help pane

claims.claim: Admin roles decide who can run diagnostics.
claims.quote: To run these diagnostics, you must meet the minimum role requirement that's listed in the table.

claims.claim: Diagnostics report known issues and provide instructions for fixing them.
claims.quote: The diagnostics offer insights into known issues, and provide instructions to fix the issues.

claims.claim: Diagnostics do not change the tenant without administrator consent.
claims.quote: Although the diagnostics can fix some configuration issues, they don't make changes to your tenant without your consent.

claims.where: What it is: Where they run, Microsoft 365 admin center row
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostics cover Exchange Online and Outlook, SharePoint and OneDrive, Teams and Purview.
claims.quote: For a full list of self-help diagnostics by product area, see the following articles: ... SharePoint Online and OneDrive ... Exchange Online and Outlook ... Microsoft Teams ... Microsoft Purview

claims.where: What it is: Where they run, Purview Help-pane row
claims.claim: Purview Help-pane diagnostics cover areas including archive mailboxes, retention, eDiscovery holds, labels, encryption and DLP.
claims.quote: The diagnostics in the Help pane cover the following areas in Microsoft Purview: Archive mailboxes; Mailbox retention; eDiscovery holds and searches; Email account security; Sensitivity labels and label policies; Email message encryption; DLP policies

claims.where: What it is: Where they run, Purview Help-pane route
claims.claim: The Purview Help-pane route starts with Help > Ask a question, then describing the issue, selecting an option and Run Tests.
claims.quote: Select the Help icon ... In the Help and support pane, select Ask a question. ... Select one of the listed options ... select Run Tests to start the diagnostic.

claims.where: What it is: Where they run, Solutions pages row
claims.claim: Purview Solutions-page diagnostics cover sensitivity labels and label policies, email encryption and DLP policies.
claims.quote: The diagnostics on Solutions pages currently cover the following areas in Microsoft Purview: Sensitivity labels and label policies; Email message encryption; Data loss prevention (DLP) policies

claims.where: What it is: Help-pane text analytics
claims.claim: Help-pane diagnostics are offered through text analytics of the problem description.
claims.quote: Describe the problem that you want to resolve, and the appropriate diagnostics are surfaced through text analytics of the problem description.

claims.where: What it is: diagnostic input values
claims.claim: Diagnostics request the values needed for the issue, such as a user name, URL or meeting ID.
claims.quote: To run a diagnostic, administrators provide specific values that are needed to troubleshoot an issue, such as a user name, URL, or Meeting ID.

claims.where: What it is: configuration data scoped to supplied values
claims.claim: Microsoft gathers configuration data scoped to supplied values for the Help-pane diagnostics generally described here.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview Help pane diagnostics data compliance boundary processing'; opened Purview self-help diagnostics and data-used-by-self-help-diagnostics. The scoped-data passage explicitly covers diagnostics running in the Microsoft 365 admin center, not both portals.
claims.fix: Replace the final sentence of this paragraph with: 'For diagnostics running in the Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft uses the supplied information to gather additional configuration data scoped to those values.'

claims.where: What it is: Solutions-page diagnostic sequence
claims.claim: A Solutions-page diagnostic first runs Check-PurviewConfig to check Purview configuration.
claims.quote: When you select a diagnostic on a Solutions page, the diagnostic runs the Check-PurviewConfig cmdlet to check your organization's configuration settings in Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: What it is: Solutions-page diagnostic sequence
claims.claim: After Check-PurviewConfig, the diagnostic calls the issue-specific cmdlet.
claims.quote: Then, the diagnostic calls the appropriate cmdlet that's listed in the following table to perform checks that are specific to your issue.

claims.where: What it is: email encryption example
claims.claim: The email-encryption diagnostic uses Test-IrmConfiguration.
claims.quote: Email encryption isn't working as expected. Are there any issues that affect my licenses or settings? ... Test-IrmConfiguration

claims.claim: The missing-label diagnostic uses Get-Label.
claims.quote: A user can't find the sensitivity label they need. Does the label policy apply to them? ... Get-label ... Get-LabelPolicy

claims.claim: The missing-label diagnostic uses Get-LabelPolicy.
claims.quote: A user can't find the sensitivity label they need. Does the label policy apply to them? ... Get-label ... Get-LabelPolicy

claims.where: What it is: DLP file example
claims.claim: The SharePoint or OneDrive DLP file-matching diagnostic uses Test-DlpPolicies.
claims.quote: A DLP rule isn't triggering for a file stored in SharePoint or OneDrive. ... Check a file's properties and classification to review whether a DLP rule matched or didn't match. ... Test-DlpPolices

claims.where: What it is: auto-labeling file example
claims.claim: The SharePoint or OneDrive auto-labeling diagnostic uses Test-DlpPolicies.
claims.quote: Autolabeling isn't applied to a SharePoint or OneDrive file. ... Checks a file's properties and classification to determine whether autolabeling was applied. ... Test-DlpPolices

claims.where: What it is: uploaded message trace
claims.claim: DLP diagnostics can use an uploaded message trace log to review DLP rules applied to Exchange Online messages.
claims.quote: A DLP rule didn't apply or it was applied unexpectedly to an email message in Exchange Online. ... Upload the message trace log (.csv) to review the DLP rules applied to email messages.

claims.where: What it is: Other uses of the word, Endpoint DLP
claims.claim: Endpoint DLP has device-health status information rather than only administrator-run self-help tests.
claims.quote: You need to understand the attributes of an onboarded device. The values for these attributes can provide useful information to help you track the device health.

claims.where: What it is: Other uses of the word, Copilot connectors
claims.claim: Copilot connectors have connection-error views distinct from self-help diagnostic tests.
claims.quote: The Error tab displays: Error codes - Lists the error codes for errors that occurred. Counts - Displays the number of occurrences for each error code. Download log - An option to download a file that lists the errors.

claims.where: Why it matters: policy and user details
claims.claim: Qualifying diagnostic users can read policy and user configuration details, including applicable DLP policies and available labels.
claims.quote: Checks which DLP policies apply to a user. Diagnostic results include the policy names and where the policies apply. ... Checks which sensitivity labels are available to the user. Diagnostic results include information such as the label names, settings

claims.where: Why it matters: Help-pane data handling; What to check
claims.claim: Help-pane diagnostics generally send tenant and user configuration outside the compliance boundary for the duration of the run.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview Help pane diagnostics data compliance boundary processing'; opened Purview diagnostics and data-used-by-self-help-diagnostics. The processing and removal statements cover Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostics, not Purview Help-pane diagnostics.
claims.fix: Replace the Why it matters sentence with: 'Diagnostics running in the Microsoft 365 admin center process tenant and user configuration outside the compliance boundary temporarily, and Microsoft says the data is removed after the diagnostic finishes.' In What to check, change 'running Help-pane diagnostics' to 'running diagnostics in the Microsoft 365 admin center'.

claims.where: Why it matters: tenant switch; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a tenant setting that independently switches self-help diagnostics off.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 self-help diagnostics disable tenant setting turn off diagnostics'. Opened Purview diagnostics, Exchange self-help diagnostics and the diagnostic data-processing page; results documented role gates but no tenant switch for these diagnostics.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no licence requirement specific to running self-help diagnostics.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Purview self-help diagnostics licensing cost price charge' and 'self-help diagnostics licensing prerequisites Microsoft 365 admin center Purview diagnostics free cost'. Read Purview and Exchange diagnostics and Purview service-description excerpts; no diagnostic-specific licence.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no charge for running self-help diagnostics.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Purview self-help diagnostics licensing cost price charge' and 'self-help diagnostics licensing prerequisites Microsoft 365 admin center Purview diagnostics free cost'. Read Purview and Exchange diagnostics and Purview service-description excerpts; no diagnostic-run price.

claims.claim: The email-encryption diagnostic checks licence availability for sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Checks license availability for sensitivity labels.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Data leaves the compliance boundary
claims.claim: Running a Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostic shows a consent notice about temporary processing and storage outside the compliance boundary.
claims.quote: When you run a self-help diagnostic in the Microsoft 365 admin center, a consent notice informs you that tenant and user configuration information will be processed and stored temporarily outside the compliance boundary.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostics can retrieve user display names.
claims.quote: Examples of tenant-defined or user-defined configuration data that might be retrieved include, but aren't limited to: ... User display names

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostics can retrieve email subject lines.
claims.quote: Examples of tenant-defined or user-defined configuration data that might be retrieved include, but aren't limited to: ... Email subject lines

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostics can retrieve SharePoint site names.
claims.quote: Examples of tenant-defined or user-defined configuration data that might be retrieved include, but aren't limited to: ... SharePoint site names

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostic service never accesses customer content such as email messages or documents.
claims.quote: Customer content such as email messages, documents, and chat conversations is never accessed by the diagnostic service.

claims.claim: Data processed for a Microsoft 365 admin center diagnostic is removed when the diagnostic finishes.
claims.quote: The data that the support systems process is automatically removed after the diagnostic process is finished. This data isn't retained for use beyond the scope of the specific diagnostic that you run.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some diagnostics offer a fix
